knownGaps: The packet lists `frontend/src/locales/**/system.json` as a file to modify; that path does not exist in this repository. Locale resources are the TypeScript files under `frontend/src/i18n/resources/`, which is where the four new keys were added. This is a path correction in the packet, not a change of intent.

The packet names `user.batch.not_found or an equivalent registered key`. `user.batch.not_found` is the batch endpoint's own key; the single-value key `user.not_found` was reused instead because it is already registered in all five locales and describes exactly one missing user. No new error key was introduced.

The packet asks for a `tenant-scoped user selector`. The candidate list is whatever `GET /system/user` returns for the `X-Tenant-Id` the request carries, which is the platform-global pool when the operator is browsing from the platform viewpoint. It is not filtered by the target tenant id, because deciding which tenant's users may join another tenant is W3/W4 scope (`scope.out`). The mismatch is surfaced in the UI with a scope notice instead of being silently resolved.

The add path validates existence only (`deleted_at IS NULL`) and stays permissive about `status`, per the packet's implementation note. A disabled user can therefore still be added; the owner-protection count is the place that requires enabled, and that asymmetry is documented in `docs/api/TENANT_API.md`.

The first full `go test -count=1 ./...` attempt in this wave was run as three concurrent invocations, which saturated the local MySQL instance: `modules/system/i18n` hit `panic: test timed out after 10m0s`. That package does not touch tenant code, so it is not a W2 regression, but the number was discarded. The authoritative reading below is a single serial run with nothing else executing.

The same concurrency left orphan `pantheon_base_test*` clone databases on the local MySQL instance (2 at the Phase 0 baseline, 23 observed while the runs were in flight). `DROP DATABASE` is destructive and was not performed; the count and the disposal decision belong to the maintainer.

The runtime screenshot was taken against the already-running dev stack (vite on 5173 serving this working tree, `pantheon-server-ops.exe` built at 13:55 on 8080). That server binary predates the handler change in this wave, so the screenshot evidences the UI selector only; the 404 envelope is evidenced by the committed mounted-route test, not by that server.

No tenant smoke fixture was brought up in this wave, so the mandatory `tenant-matrix-fixture-setup.mjs down` and `cleanup-smoke-fixtures.mjs` teardown had nothing to clean; both are recorded as not-run rather than as passes.

Credentials were read only from the gitignored root `.env.test` into the process environment of the test wrapper. No DSN, Redis password or JWT secret appears in any file in this directory; the logs here were scanned for `password=`, `@tcp(`, `PANTHEON_DSN` and `123456` before being committed.
